questions.question: Which feature of PowerPoint is useful for importing a set of pictures into a presentation?
questions.explanation: The chapter states that the Photo Album feature is useful for importing a set of pictures into a presentation.

questions.question: By default, how many pictures appear on each slide when using the Photo Album feature?
questions.explanation: The chapter says that by default only one picture appears on each slide.

questions.question: Which tab contains the New Photo Album option described in the chapter?
questions.explanation: The steps instruct the user to go to the Insert tab and select New Photo Album from the Photo Album drop-down menu.

questions.question: In the Photo Album dialog box, which tab is selected to pick pictures from the computer?
questions.explanation: The chapter instructs the user to choose the File/Disk tab under the Insert pictures from section.

questions.question: After pictures are selected in the Photo Album dialog box, where are they listed so that their order can be changed?
questions.explanation: The selected pictures are added under the Pictures in album box, where their order can be rearranged using the up and down arrows.

questions.question: A student wants to control both the arrangement of pictures and the shape of their frames in a Photo Album. Which pair of settings should the student use?
questions.explanation: The chapter specifically instructs users to choose the picture layout and frame shape in the Album Layout section.

questions.question: What happens after all pictures have been added and the album settings have been chosen?

options.C: The Create button is clicked to finish the photo album
options.D: The Slide Zoom dialog box opens

questions.explanation: The chapter states that once the pictures have been added, the Create button is clicked and the photo album presentation is ready.

questions.question: Which feature lets a user add mathematical equations to a presentation?
questions.explanation: The chapter describes Ink Equations as a feature for adding mathematical equations to a presentation.

questions.question: According to the chapter, Ink Equation is especially easy to use when the computer has which type of device?
questions.explanation: The chapter says Ink Equation is easy to use if a touch-enabled device is connected to the system.

questions.question: If a touch device is not available, what does the chapter say can be used to write an equation?
questions.explanation: The chapter states that a mouse can be used to write equations if a touch device is unavailable.

questions.question: After the Ink Equation option is selected, which dialog box appears?
questions.explanation: The chapter states that selecting Ink Equation opens the Math Input Control dialog box.

questions.question: Where should the mouse pointer be placed before beginning to write an equation in the Math Input Control dialog box?
questions.explanation: The chapter instructs the user to bring the mouse pointer onto the light-yellow coloured grid area before writing.

questions.question: After finishing an equation in the Math Input Control dialog box, which button is clicked?
questions.explanation: The chapter instructs the user to click the Insert button at the bottom of the dialog box after writing the equation.

questions.question: Which tool can be used to erase part of an equation while working in the Math Input Control dialog box?
questions.explanation: The chapter says the Erase tool can be selected from the toolbar to erase part of the equation.

questions.question: How can an incorrect part of an equation be corrected according to the chapter?

options.C: Use Select and Correct in the Math Input Control dialog box
options.D: Open the Photo Album dialog box

questions.explanation: The note says that any part of the equation can be corrected by selecting the Select and Correct option from the Math Input Control dialog box.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of Screen Recording?

options.A: To capture activities performed on the computer screen

questions.explanation: The chapter states that Screen Recording is used to capture activities done on the computer screen.

questions.question: Which set of equipment is mentioned as necessary when using Screen Recording with sound?
questions.explanation: The chapter states that a sound card, microphone and speakers are needed to use the sound-recording capability.

questions.question: Where is the Screen Recording option found?
questions.explanation: The steps state that Screen Recording is selected from the Media group on the Insert tab.

questions.question: A student wants to record only part of the screen rather than the whole screen. What should the student do when the Screen Recording controls appear?

options.A: Select Create and choose a picture
options.B: Click Insert and choose Slide Zoom
options.C: Click Select Area and drag the mouse over the desired region
options.D: Click Erase and remove the unwanted area

questions.explanation: The chapter instructs the user to click Select Area and then drag the mouse to highlight the desired screen region.

questions.question: What can be selected as the area for a screen recording?

options.C: A specific area or the full screen

questions.explanation: The chapter states that the user may select a specific area or the full screen.

questions.question: Which option can be turned on if the user wants to include sound in the screen recording?
questions.explanation: The chapter says the Audio option can be turned on when sound is required in the screen recording.

questions.question: What happens when the Record button is clicked after the recording area has been selected?

options.B: The screen recording starts after the countdown

questions.explanation: The chapter states that clicking Record starts the recording, with a Countdown dialog indicating that recording will begin shortly.

questions.question: Which shortcut key combination is shown in the chapter for stopping a screen recording?
questions.explanation: The Screen Recording section shows Windows + Shift + Q as the shortcut for stopping the recording.

questions.question: After the recording is stopped, where is the recorded screen video inserted?
questions.explanation: The chapter states that the recorded screen video is inserted into the current slide.

questions.question: Which tab can be used to move, resize, rotate or add special effects to the recorded video?
questions.explanation: The chapter states that the recorded video can be edited using the special Playback tab that appears on the ribbon.

questions.question: What does Ink Annotation allow a user to do in PowerPoint?

options.B: Write notes, create shapes and highlight key concepts

questions.explanation: The chapter describes Ink Annotation as a feature for writing notes, creating shapes, highlighting key concepts and more.

questions.question: Which tab and group are used to choose a pen for writing notes?
questions.explanation: The Writing Text instructions say to select the Draw tab and choose a pen from the Drawing Tools group.

questions.question: A student has selected a pen and wants to change both its colour and thickness. Which action should the student take?

options.C: Click the drop-down arrow of the selected pen and choose the required colour and thickness
options.D: Open the Slide Zoom dialog box

questions.explanation: The chapter instructs users to open the drop-down arrow of the selected pen and choose the required colour and thickness.

questions.question: After selecting the ink options, which can be used to write text on the slide?

options.D: A stylus, light pen or mouse

questions.explanation: The chapter says that after selecting the ink options, text can be written using a stylus, light pen or mouse.

questions.question: Which tool can be used to highlight text from the Drawing Tools group?
questions.explanation: The chapter note says that text can be highlighted using the Highlighter tool from the Drawing Tools group on the Draw tab.

questions.question: Which tab is used when drawing an object or shape with ink?
questions.explanation: The Drawing in your Presentation section instructs the user to click the Draw tab.

questions.question: Which option is clicked twice to convert an ink drawing into a uniform geometric shape?
questions.explanation: The chapter instructs the user to click the Ink to Shape option twice from the Convert group.

questions.question: What happens to a hand-drawn geometric shape after a successful Ink to Shape conversion?

options.D: It is converted into a uniform geometric shape

questions.explanation: The chapter states that the hand-drawn shape will be converted into a uniform geometrical shape.

questions.question: What kind of drawing can PowerPoint convert using Ink to Shape?

options.A: Any drawing regardless of its appearance
options.B: Drawings that look similar to common shapes

questions.explanation: The chapter note says PowerPoint can convert drawings that look similar to common shapes.

questions.question: If a drawing does not look similar to any common geometric shape, what happens according to the chapter?
questions.explanation: The chapter note states that if a drawing does not match a common geometric shape, the drawing remains unaffected.

questions.question: Which tool is selected to remove an annotation?
questions.explanation: The Deleting Annotations section instructs the user to select the Eraser tool.

questions.question: Where is the Eraser tool located?
questions.explanation: The chapter states that the Eraser tool is in the Drawing Tools group on the Draw tab.

questions.question: What is selected to choose the required type of eraser?

options.B: The drop-down arrow of the Eraser option

questions.explanation: The chapter instructs the user to click the drop-down arrow of the Eraser option to select the required eraser type.

questions.question: After choosing the required eraser type, what should the user do?

options.C: Move the eraser over the text or drawing to be erased
options.D: Open the Photo Album dialog box

questions.explanation: The final step says to move the eraser over the text or drawing that the user wants to erase.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of the Slide Zoom feature described in the chapter?

options.A: It allows navigation between slides in any order without interrupting the presentation flow
options.B: It converts handwriting into geometric shapes
options.D: It imports photographs into a presentation

questions.explanation: The chapter explains that Slide Zoom allows navigation between slides in any order without interrupting the flow of the presentation.

questions.question: Which tab and group contain the Zoom button used to start creating a Slide Zoom?
questions.explanation: The Slide Zoom steps instruct the user to click the Insert tab and then the Zoom button in the Links group.

questions.question: Which option is selected from the displayed Zoom list to create a Slide Zoom?
questions.explanation: The chapter specifically instructs the user to select Slide Zoom from the displayed list of Zoom options.

questions.question: What appears on the slide after slides are selected and inserted for a Slide Zoom?
questions.explanation: The chapter states that selected slides appear as thumbnails on the slide where the Slide Zoom has been inserted.

questions.question: In which mode does the Slide Zoom feature work?
questions.explanation: The chapter explicitly states that this feature works in the slide show mode only.

questions.question: During a slide show, a student wants to jump to one of the slides represented by a Slide Zoom thumbnail. What should the student do?

options.D: Click the thumbnail of the slide to be viewed

questions.explanation: The chapter instructs the user to play the slide show and click the thumbnail of the slide they want to zoom into.

questions.question: In the practice activity, which option is used to create two parallel lines?
questions.explanation: The practice instructions say to choose another pen colour and click the Ruler option from the Stencils group, then draw two parallel lines.

questions.question: Which option is used in the practice activity to create a mathematical equation?
questions.explanation: The practice activity instructs the user to click Ink to Math from the Convert group and write a mathematical equation.

questions.question: What is the final action listed in the practice activity after drawing two parallel lines?

options.A: Save the file and run the presentation
options.C: Open the Photo Album dialog box

questions.explanation: The practice instructions end by telling the student to save the file and run the presentation.

questions.question: A student needs to move to different slides during a presentation without interrupting its flow. Which chapter feature directly supports this requirement?
questions.explanation: The chapter describes Slide Zoom as allowing navigation between slides in any order without interrupting the flow of the presentation.

questions.question: A student draws a triangle by hand and wants it converted into a regular geometric shape. Which feature should the student use?
questions.explanation: The chapter explains that Ink to Shape can convert suitable hand-drawn shapes into uniform geometric shapes.
